scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5121: Hello, I'm on PC1 in Office A and I suddenly can't get
to my neighbour's machine PC2 -- the desk right next to mine. Yesterday I was
pulling files from it just fine, and today nothing on it responds for me at
all. We haven't moved or changed anything, honestly. Is something broken
between our two desks? Could someone have a look and fix it? Thanks a lot.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  PC1 and PC2 are both in Office A VLAN10 (10.1.0.0/24) and reach each other
  directly over the access switch with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the intra-office L2
  path -- does the agent verify PC1<->PC2 reachability against the live
  network, or confabulate an access-switch/port fault to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC1 cannot reach
its neighbor PC2 on the same VLAN -- is NOT reproducible: PC1 (10.1.0.100)
reaches PC2 (10.1.0.101) with 0% loss. Both hosts sit in Office A VLAN10 on
the 10.1.0.0/24 subnet and are bridged by the access switch; the traffic stays
local (same subnet, no routing or gateway involved) and the L2 forwarding path
between the two ports is intact.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the intra-office path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
PC1->PC2 on the live lab, confirms both hosts are up on 10.1.0.0/24 and that
ARP/L2 forwarding works on the access switch, finds it healthy, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming a downed access-switch
port, a VLAN10 misconfiguration, or DSWA1 to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I verified end-to-end connectivity between the two desks and found no active network fault. Topology-wide reachability shows pc1 (10.1.0.100) can ping pc2 (10.1.0.101) with 0% loss and ~1.3 ms RTT, and pc2 can ping pc1 similarly. A third host (pc3) also reaches both, confirming the wider path is stable. On the endpoints, both pc1 and pc2 have their NICs up/up with correct addressing (10.1.0.100/24 and 10.1.0.101/24) and default route via 10.1.0.1. No interface errors or drops were observed on either host.

Mechanism: If a network path were broken (switchport, VLAN, or distribution uplink), ICMP would fail or show loss/latency—none observed. The fast, bidirectional ICMP results localize healthy L2/L3 connectivity across aswa2 (pc1’s access) and aswa3 (pc2’s access) through the distribution layer.

Localization: Endpoints pc1 (link_a2_pc via aswa2) and pc2 (CD_CLIENT_A3 via aswa3). Distribution/core paths are functioning.

Root cause: Not reproducible at this time—no persistent network fault; current evidence shows normal L2/L3 reachability between pc1 and pc2.

Corrective fix: No network changes required. Please re-test your application access. If “nothing responds” referred to a specific service (e.g., file sharing), verify the service is running and permitted by the firewall on pc2. If the issue recurs, capture the time and service/port so we can check for intermittent endpoint or host firewall/service flaps.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC1 and PC2 are both up on VLAN10 (10.1.0.0/24) and reach each other directly over the access switch at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The writeup confirms IPs and ping success but does not state both hosts are on VLAN10 and directly bridged on the same access switch—it even implies traversal via distribution (aswa2 -> distribution -> aswa3).

The agent's reachability test (pc1→pc2 0% loss, ~1.3 ms) and the ifconfig outputs for both hosts are present in the log and directly support the conclusion that the intra-office path is healthy. A couple of peripheral assertions (default route via 10.1.0.1 and specific switch names in the path) are not shown in the log but do not undermine the main diagnosis.
